paper_metadata.title: Gravitational wave matched filtering by quantum Monte Carlo integration and quantum amplitude amplification

experiments.description: Theoretical quantum matched-filtering experiment using quantum Monte Carlo integration (QMCI) to estimate the SNR for a given template/time-shift pair, then quantum amplitude amplification (QAA) to search over template and coalescence-time indices for a pair exceeding a threshold.

algorithm.variant: QMCI-based gravitational-wave matched filtering with QAA search

hyperparameters.rho_soft: lower SNR threshold; suggested setting rho_com (e.g. 8)
hyperparameters.rho_hard: upper SNR threshold; suggested setting rho_com + 1 (e.g. 9)
hyperparameters.M: number of time-series samples / frequency bins

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Template index m and time-shift index j are placed in uniform superposition; detector-frequency data and template values are loaded via oracles into quantum registers; SNR summands are computed from real/imaginary parts and trigonometric factors.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find (m,j) such that rho_{m,j} = (2/M) * sum_k tilde{rho}_{m,j,k} exceeds a threshold; equivalently determine whether any template/time-shift pair has SNR above threshold and output one such pair.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Two-threshold scheme: guarantee detection for rho >= rho_hard with high probability and avoid false alarms for rho < rho_soft with certainty; intermediate region [rho_soft, rho_hard) may be classified either way.

problem_instance.description: Abstract gravitational-wave matched-filtering instance defined by a detector-output frequency sequence, a noise PSD, and a bank of template waveforms; no single numerical benchmark instance is executed in the paper.

dataset_specification.description: Detector output s(t) with Fourier coefficients tilde{s}(f_k); noise PSD S_n(f); template bank {tilde{Q}_m}; no specific event catalog or observation segment is used for an end-to-end run.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discrete Fourier transform of sampled detector output; one-sided PSD normalization; template normalization (Q|Q)=1; SNR rewritten as a mean over frequency-bin summands.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: The paper provides theoretical correctness and query-complexity analysis only; no numerical benchmarking or hardware execution.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: O(log Ntemp + log M + (log M + log(sigma/epsilon)) * log(sigma/epsilon) * log log(sigma/epsilon) * log(1/delta_prime))

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Load detector-output Fourier data into QRAM; compute template-dependent real and imaginary parts via arithmetic oracles; prepare uniform superpositions over template and time-shift indices.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: After QAA success, measure (m,j), compute rho_{m,j} classically by FFT as a verification step, and compare against rho_soft.

results.value: M samples / frequency bins; Ntemp template candidates

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical exhaustive template search with FFT
speedup_claims.conditions: for template search over Ntemp candidates; with r(rho_hard) > 0 or r(rho_soft)=0 cases analyzed separately; fault-tolerant quantum setting assumed
speedup_claims.caveats: Speedup is asymptotic and depends on the fraction of marked templates; qubit savings are the main advantage over the FFT-based quantum baseline.

speedup_claims.conditions: replacing FFT SNR computation with QMCI
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a qubit-count comparison, not a runtime speedup; relies on QRAM and arithmetic oracles.
The paper notes the same order in M as the FFT-based quantum method, but with much lower qubit requirements.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(M / sqrt(r(rho_hard))) up to logarithmic factors in the successful-detection regime; O(M * sqrt(Ntemp)) up to logarithmic factors when no template exceeds rho_soft
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(M log M / r(rho_th)) for exhaustive template search with FFT; O(Ntemp M log M) when no template exceeds threshold

experiments.description: Theoretical baseline quantum matched-filtering experiment from the prior work by Gao et al., using FFT-based SNR computation and QAA/Grover-style search over templates.

algorithm.variant: FFT-based matched filtering with QAA (modified from Gao et al.)

hyperparameters.M: number of time samples / frequency bins

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Template index m is prepared in uniform superposition; an FFT-based oracle computes rho_m; a comparator marks templates with rho_m >= rho_th.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find a template m such that rho_m >= rho_th, where rho_m is the maximum over coalescence-time shifts of the matched-filter SNR.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Single-threshold marking via comparator; no soft/hard threshold separation.

problem_instance.description: Abstract gravitational-wave template-bank search over intrinsic parameters only, with coalescence time optimized by FFT.

dataset_specification.description: Detector output Fourier data and template bank; no concrete event or catalog instance is run.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: FFT used to compute rho_{m,j} for all j for each template m; then rho_m = max_j rho_{m,j}.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: The paper reports only asymptotic query complexity, not empirical evaluation.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: FFT-based computation of rho_m for each template; comparator construction; uniform superposition over templates.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure the template register; verify rho_m classically by FFT.

results.value: M time samples / frequency bins; Ntemp templates

classical_baselines.method_name: classical exhaustive template search with FFT
classical exhaustive template search with FFT

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical exhaustive template search with FFT
speedup_claims.conditions: when r(rho_th) > 0; and in the no-signal case r(rho_th)=0
speedup_claims.caveats: The quantum algorithm still requires O(M) qubits because FFT computes all coalescence-time shifts simultaneously.

scalability_data.metric_value: O(sqrt(Ntemp) M log M) when r(rho_th)=0

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(M log M / sqrt(r(rho_th))) when r(rho_th) > 0; O(sqrt(Ntemp) M log M) when r(rho_th) = 0
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(M log M / r(rho_th)) when r(rho_th) > 0; O(Ntemp M log M) when r(rho_th) = 0

experiments.description: Illustrative numerical study of the template-shape parameter gamma for compact-binary-coalescence waveforms, used to justify the bounded-variance assumption in the proposed algorithm.

algorithm.variant: parameter-sweep evaluation of gamma for CBC templates

problem_formulation.objective_function: Compute gamma = max_{m,k} |Q_m(f_k)| / sqrt(S_n(f_k) Delta t) over a CBC waveform family.

problem_instance.description: Compact binary coalescence waveform family used to evaluate gamma across masses and mass ratios.

dataset_specification.description: Templates computed from IMRPhenomPv2; spins fixed to zero; total masses from 1 to 300 solar masses; mass ratios from 0.2 to 1; Advanced LIGO design sensitivity PSD.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Evaluate template amplitude distribution over frequency bins and compute gamma from the normalized template spectrum.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single-figure parameter sweep; no statistical averaging or repeated runs reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute template spectra from the IMRPhenomPv2 model and normalize by the Advanced LIGO PSD.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Report gamma values; minimum gamma 2.50 and maximum gamma 4.66 in the scanned parameter region.

speedup_claims.caveats: This is a classical parameter-sweep figure used to justify the bounded-variance assumption, not a quantum-vs-classical benchmark.
